{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1794699823295,"sessionID":"ses_e238e7e4bffeie9oQStcZNxbkI","part":{"id":"prt_1dc71d1ed001qLe2ctQKkDl85S","messageID":"msg_1dc71c311001GGiifwfwJWz1bS","sessionID":"ses_e238e7e4bffeie9oQStcZNxbkI","type":"reasoning","text":"**Calculating Beam Paths**\n\nI've determined the exit positions for both beams. The 800nm beam exits at z=205, height=124, while the OPA beam (600nm) exits at z=804, height=159. They are both traveling towards -x (yaw=180). Based on these exit positions, the path length difference is 1879 mm. The 800nm path requires an additional 1879 mm of table path. I made a correction to this figure: internal path for 800nm = 6.\n\n\n**Planning Table Layout**\n\nI'm now focusing on the table layout, needing to accommodate a significant 1879 mm path difference for the 800nm beam. I'm considering using a delay stage (DL-C100 seems like the best option for the range) and a retroreflector to achieve this. The retroreflector adds twice the distance from the entrance to its apex to the path length. I'm working with the table's dimensions, 2400 mm in x and 1200 mm in z, to map out a suitable path for the 800nm beam, which starts at (2250, 205).\n\n\n**Revising Beam Paths**\n\nI'm now revising the beam paths, particularly the height matching. Initially, I considered a periscope for the OPA beam to align heights, but now I'm thinking of bringing the OPA to the same height. Coarse delay can be done using table geometry to make path(OPA) + 1879 mm = path(800nm). I calculated path(OPA) as 1750 mm to the sample. The beams can enter the lens at points separated by, say, 10 mm.\n\n\n**Refining Path Alignment**\n\nI've decided to incorporate a periscope for the OPA beam to ensure height alignment. The OPA beam originates at (2250, 804) with a height of 159, and is traveling in the -x direction.
